data.turoyo: Aṯi zaman, aḥna, as səryoye, d maqbelna i mšiḥoyuṯo, d kətwa əšmayna oromoye, d fliġina, d hawina tre gabe. L gabe maqbele i səry... i mšiḥoyuṯo w u gabo ḥreno fayəš bi puṭparastiye, bi waṯaniye.
data.translation: A time came when we Syriac Christians accepted Christianity, when our name was Arameans, when we divided and became two sides. One side accepted Syriac... Christianity, and the other side remained in idolatry, in paganism.

rationale: New Detransitive Preterit box; fliġina and became two sides make finite reciprocal division explicit. Jan translation is project machine translation, quoted verbatim; analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 4.II/1006)

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1b in Preterit (Jan 3.56/1638)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr mayo li katolikiye mḥela šalqe li mšiḥoyuṯo di səryoyuṯo. Mawbelala qəsm mina. Fliġi ann aḥunonayḏan aʕlayna w mawballe qəsm šan ruḥayye.
data.translation: After that, Catholicism dealt a blow to Syriac Christianity. It took a part of it away. These brothers of ours separated from us and took a part for themselves.

rationale: Single clear example of the new Detransitive secession construction, distinct from active round-1 separation with m-. Jan translation is project machine translation, quoted verbatim; analysis rests on Turoyo.

data.translation: Then I had sent him one last year. And I had taken it, I had also given it to Cemal Gürsel, when I went to Ankara. I had done that with it, I had distributed it among the pashas and among the presidents, among the military too and among the religious community too.

data.translation: Consecrated sister Mahbe: Then they break that bread and look to see to whose lot it falls. Then, if it has come out—now they are rozune—they will divide them up; they will give one to me, so that I give one to my husband; I will give some to my children. And now, this year, it has fallen to my husband.

rationale: First II Infectum example; gəd- and ensuing future giving distinguish the form from homographic Preterit. Jan translation is project machine translation, quoted verbatim; analysis rests on Turoyo.

data.translation: Bishop Hanna and the other priests become disturbed over what Father Aziz did. Bishop Hanna quickly suspends Father Aziz from the priesthood. The priests divide, and there is turmoil among the Syriacs.

rationale: Fifth Detransitive Infectum example; contemporary factional division supports the social range already noted in round 1. Jan translation is project machine translation, quoted verbatim; analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: Restore corpus ʕam before am=miṯe
rationale: 25/65 reads fləġli ak kallatani kulle ʕam am miṯe. The quotation substitutes ʕal for ʕam, changing the preposition's final consonant. Preserve the normalized article boundary am=miṯe while restoring the corpus word.

summary: Restore ṣ in ʕaṣro (ten)
rationale: The cited verse has ʕaṣro kallat, with emphatic ṣ. The supplied dictionary also lists ʕaṣro as ten. The quotation has plain s, a consonant transcription error.

summary: Active separation with m- (PrS 13/13; 95/4) is distinct from transitive apportionment. Political spitting of a community (Lahdo interviews) is a figurative specialisation; the two interviews describe the same legal allegation, not independent historical events.

Distribution recipients occur with ʕal and l-, co-participants with ʕam. Postverbal l-NPs can be agents: PrS 77/25 names the fox and dog as joint dividers, so l- must not automatically be labelled recipient.

Detransitive Infinitiv floġ is retained in its inherited box even when it names the active skill of dividing. Part. Pass. flíġewayne expresses a divided state; Infectum Koməfloġi describes a group dividing itself.

New Infectum-wa and Preterit-wa boxes contrast habitual allocation and anterior completed division. Bare flaġən addressed to a singular animal is Imperativ, correcting the reader’s isolated inclusive-Infectum analysis at PrS 82/19.

Read-only lookup confirms plġ has a single I Preterit division example and the same MEA etymology. The p/f alternation warrants editorial cross-reference review, but no wholesale merger or replacement of spelling is proposed.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the supplied Turoyo; retained English quotations are verbatim machine translation. Only round-2 changes are encoded here.
Keep the independently numbered active and Detransitive sense lists distinct: active 1b and 2 are inherited round-1 proposals; new Detransitive 1b is a construction under its own sense 1.
New finite boxes here are I Detransitive Preterit and Infectum-wa, II Infectum and Infectum-wa. I Part. Pass. already exists in round 1; Jan examples only fill that remaining thin cell.
The three kmifalġi tokens at Jan 3.56/1679 contrast with active mfalġinanne, but II versus I Detransitive is unresolved. No II Detransitive box is published from provisional vocalism alone.
The parenthetic fliġe at Jan 3.55/1545 is Jan’s editorial explanation of Turkish ayrı, not secure spoken morphology. It confirms the separated meaning without adding a quotation.
No new idiom is established. The heart/doubt question from round 1 is not resolved by Jan and is not turned into a proposed sense here.
At 113/5, does fliġ lebe mean doubt, inward division, or another state? The supplied German is corrupt (etwas 00an Gott. zweifelte); verify before adding an idiom or sense.
Collate 25/65: entry has ʕal-am=miṯe, supplied verse has ʕam am miṯe. No automatic text correction is justified without the edition.
Confirm segmentation of Flaġe, kfolaġnən, fliġəlle and fliġənne; retain exact spelling. PrS 82/25 has singular-looking Fləġle against a plural German subject.
Should the p/f spelling entries plġ and flġ be cross-referenced or consolidated? Keep old prs page/line references distinct from supplied text/verse numbers until concordance is checked.
At Jan 3.56/1679, does mi-falġ- establish II Detransitive or represent a variant of I məfləġ? Confirm stem before adding a box.
Parse II mfalaġwayne at Jan 3.18/401, including person/object sequence and the -wa position; Infectum-wa placement is provisional.
At Jan 3.24/610, do fliġe wən and ʕal denote allegiance to competing patrons? The Part. Pass. divided-state analysis is secure, the social details are not.
Confirm that ʕal in Jan 3.56/1638 marks the group separated from; the new secession subsense rests on this overt contrast and taking a part for themselves.
Division/distribution applies to troops, marriage partners, food, merchandise and inheritances, as well as money; participant changes do not establish separate meanings.
Detransitive includes general divisibility, reflexive formation of groups and resultant factional division.
External recipients may be l-marked, besides reciprocal ʕal ruḥayye / ʕal ḥḏoḏe.
Classification of narratives and book sections is an abstract participant/result extension of divide. The l- complement names resulting categories; it does not name recipients.
Active political division of east from west is related to round-1 political splitting; no second political sense is introduced.
Detransitive factional and territorial division supports round 1’s reciprocal/state analysis. Railway-route divergence extends the divided participant without a new numbered meaning.
Dividing a written book and distributing copies apply the existing sense to textual objects. Jan also supplies II Infectum and Infectum-wa, absent after round 1.
